articles.title: Philip Rivers Hires Former NFL Assistant Coach as NC State Offensive Coordinator
articles.summary: NC State has hired Jason Michael as the team's offensive coordinator under new head coach Philip Rivers, the school announced Wednesday.
articles.body:
NC State has hired Jason Michael as the team's offensive coordinator under new head coach Philip Rivers, the school announced Wednesday.

Rivers, who played for the Wolfpack in college before earning eight Pro Bowl nods across his NFL career with the Los Angeles Chargers and Indianapolis Colts, was officially hired as the head coach of his alma mater on Nov. 11.

"I'm really excited to add coach Michael to our staff," Rivers said, per the school's official website . "I have history with him from my time with the Chargers and with the Colts and we are aligned in our vision for building this program. His expertise and experience in the offensive system that we are going to implement here at NC State is second to none, and I can't wait for him to get started."

Michael has coached at the NFL level since 2009, recently operating as the Philadelphia Eagles' tight ends coach from 2021-25.

He has familiarity with Rivers, serving as the Chargers' tight ends coach alongside the star quarterback from 2011-13. Michael was also a member of the Colts' coaching staff in 2020 while Rivers was with the team.

Michael has two years of experience as an offensive coordinator, filling the role for the Tennessee Titans from 2014-15.

The Titans struggled during his tenure, ranking No. 30 among all NFL teams in scoring offense during the 2014 season before ranking No. 28 in 2015.

NC State is looking to establish itself as a threat in the ACC under Rivers after compiling a mere 18-18 record since the start of the 2024 season. That includes a 4-6 mark this year.

articles.title: Juliano Belletti hits back at claims Jesse Bisiwu is struggling to adapt at Barcelona
articles.summary: The coach has backed the summer signing.
articles.body:
Bisiwu impressed in pre-season and had been expected to share game time with Belletti's men and Hansi Flick's first team this season.

An early injury disrupted his progress and there has been talk he's struggling to settle. Belletti's been asked about such talk and insisted the youngster is doing fine.

"Who said that? From day one he has been adapted, very happy and very happy to be with us. In every training session he listens, asks questions, tries to adapt to the way of playing, especially since we have wingers in width, which comes a bit inside," he told Sport.

"He is searching, asking, and I always see very good intentions on his part as well, especially in defensive transitions.

"He is adapting to our way of playing and evolving a lot, especially as a footballer, in the discipline of playing without the ball. Not integrated? On the contrary, here in our daily lives, Bisiwu is adapted and very happy."

articles.title: Fred Warner's heritage makes 49ers' upcoming game in Mexico City special
articles.summary: (AP) — San Francisco has a history with Mexico, having played there in 2022, while 49ers linebacker Fred Warner has roots in the country.Warner’s maternal gr...
articles.body:
AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. (AP) — San Francisco has a history with Mexico, having played there in 2022, while 49ers linebacker Fred Warner has roots in the country.

Warner's maternal grandfather was born in Mexico but died when Warner's mother, Laura, was young. Although he never met his grandfather, Warner has spoken in the past about his connection to Mexican culture, including speaking Spanish in his childhood home.

San Francisco plays the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday night, and Warner is excited to return.

"Super special," he said after practice on Wednesday. "I remember that first time around, didn't know what exactly what to expect, but I think that was my first time being out of the country and playing in a game of that magnitude."

Warner attended a World Cup game at Estadio Azteca last summer and found the atmosphere electric.

"That was elite," said Warner, who leads the team in tackles with 88. "Soccer, or football as they call it, the World Cup, representing your home country, that is a whole different animal. The NFL obviously is elite as well, but that was that was a once-in-a-lifetime experience."

San Francisco beat Arizona 38-10 in Mexico City on Nov. 21, 2022, and the team is following the same blueprint to prepare for Sunday night's game. After beating Dallas last Sunday, the 49ers flew to Colorado so they could practice at the Air Force Academy, where the 7,258-foot elevation is nearly equal to Mexico City, hoping to gain an advantage for the NFL's final international game of 2026.

They hope some things are different from four years ago.

"Usually our last bus of players gets three hours before the game, and they got lost somehow on the way to the stadium," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "They didn't get there until an hour and 15 minutes before the game, and had like 12 starters on it. So that was somewhat stressful, but it didn't affect us.

"After the game it took us about 10 hours to get out of there, just because we had to wait through customs for the Cardinals to go first, so we got back the next Tuesday morning at like 9 a.m. because we played on a Monday night. The stadium was awesome. The atmosphere is great. It was a really cool place to play football."

Evans could return to practice soon and other injury news

Wide receiver Mike Evans did not practice Wednesday but has not been ruled out for Sunday night, Shanahan said. Evans, who has missed the last three games with Achilles tendinitis, is third on the team in catches (39) and receiving yards (420) despite playing in just six of nine games.

"Hopefully he'll be able to go (Thursday)," Shanahan said. "I'm not sure yet, but taking it day by day right now."

Evans did some work with two coaches in pre-practice warmups, lightly jogging while catching passes near the sideline on a windy afternoon.

Evans, in his first season with San Francisco, has made an impact when available, most notably his seven catches for 113 yards and a score in a Week 5 win at Seattle despite playing with a rib injury.

Shanahan was asked if Evans' presence in Colorado means there's hope he can play Sunday night.

"Haven't thought about that," he said. "Maybe, but he does have a chance. But, if he didn't, probably still would've brought him."

Linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) also did not practice but Shanahan said he is likely to practice Thursday. Cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Upton Stout (shoulder), safeties Ji'Ayir Brown (ankle) and Siran Neal (foot) and defensive end Khalid Kareem (ankle) were limited.

articles.title: Miami Hurricanes Must Win To Secure Playoff Spot
articles.summary: Miami sits at No. 7 but needs the ACC title for a playoff bid. Can the Canes handle Virginia Tech and Boston College to keep their dream alive?
articles.body:
Following Saturday's 36-25 victory against Duke, the Miami Hurricanes remain fixed at No. 7 in the newest College Football Playoff rankings. The Selection Committee revealed these numbers on Tuesday, and the Canes did not move up. Notre Dame and Texas swapped spots, but Miami stayed put. The team lost to Notre Dame 31-24 earlier in the season, and that loss to the only ranked opponent on their schedule hurts their case. They need a clear path forward to make the playoff.

Winning the Atlantic Coast Conference title is the only sure way to get an automatic bid. Under the 12 team format the four highest ranked conference champions earn a first-round bye, which Miami in that position if it wins the league. The path is narrow. Wake Forest sits at No. 11 after a huge 49-7 win over SMU. Were the playoffs to begin now, the Demon Deacons would secure the final spot via an at-large bid. Miami has to beat teams in front of them to climb higher.

Maintaining an undefeated conference record, Miami retains the opportunity to reach the playoff for a second consecutive year. They face Virginia Tech on Nov. 21 and Boston College on Nov. 28. Both games are at Hard Rock Stadium. According to reports, the Canes hold better than a 95% probability of winning both upcoming games. That is a good sign, but the stats do not guarantee a win on the field.

Should Miami finish the regular season undefeated yet fall in the conference title game, their likelihood of securing an at-large bid probably vanishes. An ACC champion carrying two non-conference losses will struggle to earn votes from the committee. The team must win the ACC Championship to lock in a spot. They appeared in the title game in 2017 but lost to Clemson 38-3. They have never won that game.

Wide receiver Malachi Toney remains unavailable for the Hurricanes due to ankle surgery. He is a star player, and his health matters for the final stretch. The dream is to have him back for the semifinals or a potential rematch with Notre Dame. The committee chair Hunter Yurachek said, "It's hard for me to sit here with two weeks left in the regular season and of course championship weekend to say what can happen with Miami in the rankings and those above them," according to Sports Illustrated .

Yurachek also noted that losses by teams above Miami would help the Canes as long as they keep winning. He added, "Obviously, if there's some movement or losses in teams above them, that helps them as long as they continue to win. Then of course if they advance to the ACC championship game, if it is indeed Wake Forest, they have an opportunity against a ranked team on championship weekend." The Hurricanes will aim to win the ACC Championship in Charlotte, N.C. on Dec. 5, 2026.

If they win the title game and finish as one of the top-four conference champions, they get a bye in the first round and set their first playoff game for New Year's. That gives the team more rest while other talented players come out of the injury booth. The committee says Miami will likely stay in the six-to-eight range unless something drastic happens.

articles.title: Utah Royals' Jimmy Coenraets wins NWSL coach of the year
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Utah Royals head coach Jimmy Coenraets won the 2026 National Women’s Soccer League Coach of the Year after a remarkable turnaround for a c...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Utah Royals head coach Jimmy Coenraets won the 2026 National Women's Soccer League Coach of the Year after a remarkable turnaround for a club that went from one of the NWSL's worst teams to a playoff team in the space of a season.

The 31-year-old Belgian beat out San Diego Wave head coach Jonas Eidevall and Gotham FC's Juan Carlos Amorós for the honor, announced Wednesday during the league's annual awards ceremony at Lisner Auditorium in Washington, D.C.

The Belgian is hardly a conventional coach.

Coenraets played soccer growing up but could not complete his dreams of becoming a pro because of a heart condition. He then studied marketing and has a master's degree in strategy and international football business. While initially inclined to focus on the business of soccer, his passion for the sport eventually led him to coach for OH Leuven in Belgium.

When the assistant coach offer came from Utah's then-sporting director, Kelly Cousins, he jumped at the opportunity.

Coenraets, one of the youngest head coaches in the league, guided the Royals to their first playoff appearance since the franchise returned to the NWSL in 2024 after finishing 12th in the standings last season. Utah produced one of the biggest upsets of the postseason, eliminating the higher-seeded Wave in the quarterfinals before falling 2-1 to the Washington Spirit in Saturday's semifinal.

But the team's transformation began long before the playoffs.

Coenraets inherited a club struggling to establish itself after its 2023 relocation. The Royals struggled to sign big stars, but rather than relying on established standouts, Coenraets focused on building a collective identity, developing younger players and instilling a competitive mentality that made Utah increasingly difficult to beat.

"If you look at the way we play as a team right now, that's not 100 percent how I'm used to playing," Coenraets told The Athletic earlier this year. "But it does suit what we have, where we are as a franchise, and it suits within the plan of where we want to go."

The Royals emerged as one of the surprises of the regular season, climbing into the upper reaches of the standings and establishing themselves as legitimate postseason contenders. Coenraets was named NWSL Coach of the Month in May, an early indication of the progress his team was making.
